key_insight: Gemini achieved the highest accuracy (90.29%), but SVM and the strongest transformer showed no statistically significant difference, cautioning against claims of model-family superiority.
clinical_relevance: Classifying informal Bangla patient narratives could support specialty referral workflows, but clinical utility and safety remain unproven.
method: Compared 6 classical ML models, 4 deep learning models, 4 fine-tuned transformers, and 5 zero-shot LLMs.
Used 2,730 patient records across Medicine, Gynecology, Dermatology, Pediatrics, and Gastroenterology with a shared 80:20 train–test split.
Assessed performance and pairwise differences using Holm-corrected McNemar tests.
evidence_signal: Best-in-family accuracy was 90.29% for Gemini, 86.26% for XLM-RoBERTa, 84.98% for SVM, and 80.77% for Bidirectional GRU; the Gemini–Grok difference was not significant after correction.
watch_item: Evaluation covered only the five most represented specialties from a 20-specialty corpus, limiting generalization to broader referral settings.
paper_title: Medical Specialty Prediction from Bangla Patient Narratives: A Comparative Study of ML, DL, Transformers, and LLMs
